chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding

the woman who sees the yellowness: so he said: 'If it was before the menstruation by two days, then it is from the menstruation; and if it was after the menstruation by two days, then it is not from the menstruation.'

key_terms.الصُّفْرَة: Sufra — yellowish discharge, a form of istihadha or transitional blood that requires juristic classification
key_terms.الْحَيْض: Haydh — menstruation, a specific state of ritual impurity in Islamic law that suspends certain worship obligations

ai.seo_question: Is yellowish discharge before or after menstruation considered part of haydh in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a legal ruling on the status of yellowish discharge (sufra) in relation to menstruation: if it appears within two days before the onset of menstruation, it is considered part of the menstrual blood; if it appears two days after menstruation ends, it is not counted as menstrual blood. This ruling has important implications for ritual purity obligations, as it determines whether a woman is in a state of haydh (menstruation) requiring abstention from prayer and fasting.
